patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient reports a 6-week history of tingling pain in the sole of his right foot, which worsens when he raises it above chest level during exercises. He mentions that he began exercising regularly 2 months ago and experiences right calf cramps with the use of the treadmill's incline feature, necessitating frequent breaks. The pain subsides completely after a few minutes of resting. He adds an 8-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Tingling pain in the sole of the right foot upon elevation

patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Smokes two packs of cigarettes daily for 34 years.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with tingling pain in the sole of the right foot, especially upon elevation and during exercise, with a significant history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and smoking.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “About six weeks ago I started getting a tingling, painful feeling in the sole of my right foot. It seems to worsen when I raise my foot above chest level during exercise, and when I rest for a few minutes it completely goes away.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any swelling in your joints?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any swelling or joint problems. The main issue is the tingling, painful feeling in the sole of my right foot, especially when I lift it higher during exercise.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual spots on your scalp?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual spots on my scalp.” “This has mainly been limited to the tingling painful feeling in the sole of my right foot.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itching or a persistent urge to scratch anywhere on your body?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had itching or an urge to scratch anywhere. My symptoms have stayed focused on the tingling, painful feeling in the sole of my right foot, and it clears up after a few minutes of rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any trouble lifting your arms above your head?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I don’t have trouble lifting my arms above my head. This problem has been mainly in the sole of my right foot, and it eases completely after a few minutes of rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any loss of vision that isn’t accompanied by pain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any vision loss—no spots, blurring, or anything like that, with or without pain. My symptoms are only in the sole of my right foot and they go away after a few minutes of rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had a fever that’s felt extremely hot—like a temperature above 104 °F (40 °C) that’s made you feel dizzy or very uncomfortable?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any fever or feeling extremely hot like that, and I haven’t had dizziness with these symptoms.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately?
turns.patient_answer: “Not really—nothing unusual beyond starting the treadmill incline workouts a couple of months ago. The symptoms seem tied to raising my right foot during exercise, and then they go away after I stop and rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced any burning or discomfort when you urinate?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any burning or discomfort when I urinate. My main issue has been the tingling pain in the sole of my right foot, which comes on with raising it during exercise and disappears after a few minutes of rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling chills lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had chills or any flu-like symptoms. My main complaint is still the tingling, painful feeling in the sole of my right foot that shows up with raising my foot during exercise and clears after a few minutes of rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any lumps or masses in your breasts that feel fixed or don’t move?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any lumps or masses in my breasts. This whole problem has been limited to the tingling, painful feeling in the sole of my right foot with exercise, and it goes away after a few minutes of rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling any pain or discomfort on the side of your back or abdomen, between your ribs and hips?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any pain or discomfort in my back or abdomen between my ribs and hips. The discomfort is mainly in the sole of my right foot and it improves completely after I rest for a few minutes.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel pain in your calf when you walk, and does it go away when you stop and rest?
turns.patient_answer: “Yes—when I use the treadmill incline, I get cramps/pain in my right calf, and I have to stop for a bit; after a few minutes of rest it eases completely.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your urine looks darker than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed my urine looking darker than usual. My main issue is the tingling, painful feeling in the sole of my right foot and the right calf cramps with the incline treadmill, which both improve completely after a few minutes of rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you find it hard to lift your arm above your head or reach across your body?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I don’t find it hard to lift my arms above my head or reach across my body. The problem stays in the sole of my right foot when I raise it during exercise, and it clears up after a few minutes of rest.”
